problem_motivation.content: There is a need for high temperature structural materials with superior oxidation resistance.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: In consideration of the superior oxidation resistance

problem_motivation.content: High-entropy refractory alloys (RHEAs) are bottlenecked by high density and poor high-temperature oxidation resistance, limiting their use as structural materials.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: However, most of these RHEAs are generally characterized with high density and poor high temperature oxidation resistance. Such drawbacks are the current bottleneck for utilizing RHEAs as structural materials.

prior_approach.content: Previous studies utilized the arc melting process to prepare RHEAs, resulting in as-cast alloys with dendritic structures.
prior_approach.evidence_span: As reported in the literature, most of the RHEAs were prepared by the arc melting process. These as-cast alloys generally exhibited a dendritic structure with severe composition segregation

prior_approach.content: Literature references cite the use of reinforcement particles like carbides, oxides, and nitrides in metal matrix composites.
prior_approach.evidence_span: The reinforcement particles include carbides (TiC, SiC), oxides (Al 2 O 3 , Y 2 O 3 ), nitrides, (Si 3 N 4 , BN), and borides (TiB 2 , LaB 6 ).

prior_approach.content: Previous studies established empirical rules for BCC phase formation in HEAs based on VEC, delta, and Omega parameters.
prior_approach.evidence_span: According to the empirical rules, BCC solid solutions were generally formed in HEA systems under the following certain conditions.

prior_approach.content: Prior work compared the mechanical properties of HEAs with ceramic reinforcements like TiC and SiC.
prior_approach.evidence_span: As listed in Table 3 , the yield strength of (FeCrNiCo)Al 0.7 Cu 0.5 base HEA reached 630 MPa accompanied by a high strain of 42.7%.

prior_limitation.content: The as-cast NbMoCrTiAl HEA has lower compressive fracture strength compared to the composite.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: compared with that of the as-cast NbMoCrTiAl HEA

prior_limitation.content: The specifically designed equiatomic NbMoCrTiAl RHEA exhibits insufficient high-temperature strength despite good oxidation resistance.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: However, the compressive strength of the as-cast NbMoCrTiAl alloy was reported to be as low as 1010 MPa and its high temperature strength is insufficient.

prior_limitation.content: Arc melting preparation methods result in dendritic structures and severe composition segregation.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: most of the RHEAs were prepared by the arc melting process. These as-cast alloys generally exhibited a dendritic structure with severe composition segregation

prior_limitation.content: Prior empirical rules predicted ductility based on VEC, but the current material is brittle despite fitting the criteria.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: Guo et al. [ [28] ] further proposed that all ductile alloys have a VEC ≤ 4.4, while all brittle alloys have a VEC ≥ 4.6. Therefore, the NbMoCrTiAl RHEA should be without ductility and it is indeed a type of brittle RHEA.

prior_limitation.content: Previous studies noted that plastic strain drops significantly when ceramic reinforcements are added.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: With the addition of 10 vol. % TiC, the yield strength increased to 1290 MPa, while plastic strain dropped to 29.2% [ [31] ].

causal_claim.content: The presence of approximately 7.0 vol. % Al2O3 and 32.2 vol. % TiC reinforced particles resulted in an approximately 50% increase in compressive fracture strength.
causal_claim.evidence_span: With the presence of approximately 7.0 vol. % Al 2 O 3 and 32.2 vol. % TiC reinforced particles, the compressive fracture strength of the composite (1542 MPa) was increased by approximately 50%

causal_claim.content: The introduction of brittle ceramic reinforcements significantly increased the mechanical properties of the material.
causal_claim.evidence_span: It can be found that introduction of brittle ceramic reinforcements would significantly increase mechanical properties of the material.

causal_claim.content: The addition of interstitial carbon led to an increase in yield strength and elongation to fracture in a previous study.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Wang et al. [ [33] , [34] ] reported that the addition of 1.1 at. % carbon to a novel single-phase FCC Fe 40.4 Ni 11.3 Mn 34.8 Al 7.5 Cr 6 HEA not only markedly increased the yield strength from 159 MPa to 355 MPa, but also led to a 25 % increase in the elongation to fracture.

mechanism_principle.content: The high solubility of Nb-carbide in TiC is due to the large negative mixing enthalpy and identical crystal structure.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: this certain concentration of Nb incorporated during grain growth agrees with the large solubility of solute Nb-carbide in solvent TiC mainly because of their largest negative value of Hmix and identical crystal structure.

mechanism_principle.content: The inability of Mo, Cr, and Al to dissolve in TiC is attributed to weak cohesive forces.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: While Mo, Cr, and Al could not dissolve in the TiC due to their relatively weak cohesive force [ [30] ].

mechanism_principle.content: Grain refinement occurs because the powder metallurgy process is more effective at refining grains than arc-melting.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This is because the PM process is an effective approach to refine grains compared to arc-melting [ [16] ].

mechanism_principle.content: Hard phases at grain boundaries act as barriers that suppress grain growth.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: In addition, the hard phases evenly distributed at the grain boundary, acting as the barrier of grain growth.

mechanism_principle.content: Interstitial atoms cause significant strengthening by creating strain fields that interact with gliding dislocations.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: These interstitial atoms will produce a substantial strain field, with which gliding dislocations will interact.

mechanism_principle.content: The expansion of the TiC lattice constant is likely caused by the solution of large atoms like Nb.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The different crystal parameter may result from the solution of atoms with large radius, such as element Nb (r = 0.148 nm) in this composite.

hypothesis_statement.content: The P/M NbMoCrTiAl high entropy alloy composite is proposed as a promising high temperature structural material due to its superior oxidation resistance.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: the P/M NbMoCrTiAl high entropy alloy composite could be considered as a promising high temperature structural material

hypothesis_statement.content: The authors conclude that the solution-strengthening effect is responsible for the improved mechanical properties.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Therefore, we may reasonably conclude that solution-strengthening effect resulted in the improved mechanical properties.

evidence_result.content: The composite achieved a fracture strength of 1542 MPa, which is more than 50% higher than the as-cast alloy.
evidence_result.evidence_span: the fracture strength of the composite was 1542 MPa, increasing by more than a half than that of the as-cast alloy (1010 MPa)

evidence_result.content: The composite exhibits a typical cleavage fracture mode without ductility, confirmed by the river pattern observed on the fracture surface.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Cleavage fracture is featured by river pattern, which could be clearly seen in Figure 5 . This means that the NbMoCrTiAl HEA composite shows typical cleavage fracture mode without ductility.

evidence_result.content: The average particle sizes for TiC and Al2O3 were measured as approximately 4.60 μm and 1.57 μm, respectively.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The average particle size of TiC and Al 2 O 3 were measured to be approximately 4.60 μm and 1.57 μm, respectively.

evidence_result.content: The composite achieved a compressive strength of 1542 MPa.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The composite created a kind of material with highly improved compressive strength (1542 MPa)

evidence_result.content: The as-cast NbMoCrTiAl alloy had a compressive strength of 1010 MPa.
evidence_result.evidence_span: compared with that of the as-cast NbMoCrTiAl alloy (1010 MPa).

evidence_result.content: Microstructural analysis revealed a typical cleavage fracture mode in the composite.
evidence_result.evidence_span: On the basis of microstructure features of the fracture surface, typical cleavage fracture mode was found in the composite.

evidence_result.content: No apparent debonding was observed between the dispersed particles and the HEA matrix.
evidence_result.evidence_span: No apparent debonding between dispersed particles and the HEA matrix could be found

constraint.content: The stearic acid was introduced as a process control agent with a specific empirical dosage to prevent cold welding and agglomeration while acting as a reinforcement additive.
constraint.evidence_span: The empirical addition amount of stearic acid was 3.5 wt. %. The stearic acid was introduced as process control agent (PCA) to prevent cold welding as well as particle agglomeration, and also acted as additive for generating particulate reinforced HEA composite.

constraint.content: The SPS consolidation process was constrained to specific axial pressure, temperature, heating rate, and holding time.
constraint.evidence_span: under 30 MPa axial pressure at 1700 °C with the heating rate of 100 K/min. During the sintering process, the sample was held at the sintering temperature for 30 min.

constraint.content: The Vickers microhardness measurement was constrained to a specific indenter load and holding time.
constraint.evidence_span: with an indenter load of 100 g and the holding time was 15 s.

constraint.content: The compression tests were constrained to a specific specimen geometry, strain rate, and ambient temperature condition.
constraint.evidence_span: Cylindrical specimens of compression tests (4 mm in diameter and 6 mm in height) were cut and machined from the sintered bulk. Room temperature compression tests were carried out on an Instron-3369 (INSTRON, Norwood, MA, USA) universal testing machines at strain rate of 10 −3 s −1 .
